Statistics, machine learning and genomics

This vignette covers the statistical, machine-learning and genomics functions. Like the plotting family, the statistical and ML functions return a ggplot by default and a tidy data frame (with the fitted model attached as an attribute) when return.data = TRUE. For the figure functions see vignette("visualization", package = "micropubr").

library(micropubr)
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
gp <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(
  phyloseq::taxa_sums(GlobalPatterns) > 5, GlobalPatterns)

# GlobalPatterns has no numeric covariates; add a few synthetic ones so the
# Mantel and variance-partitioning examples have something to chew on.
set.seed(1)
meta <- data.frame(phyloseq::sample_data(gp))
meta$pH    <- round(runif(nrow(meta), 5, 8), 1)
meta$Temp  <- round(runif(nrow(meta), 4, 37), 1)
meta$Depth <- round(runif(nrow(meta), 0, 100), 1)
phyloseq::sample_data(gp) <- phyloseq::sample_data(meta)

Multivariate dispersion (PERMDISP)

mp_dispersion() tests whether group dispersions (spread around the centroid) differ, the assumption behind PERMANOVA. Add ANOSIM/MRPP/PERMANOVA to the caption with add.test.

mp_dispersion(gp, group.by = "SampleType", add.test = "permanova")

Mantel test

mp_mantel() correlates the community distance matrix with a distance built from numeric metadata.

mp_mantel(gp, vars = c("pH", "Temp", "Depth"), method = "spearman")

Variance partitioning

mp_varpart() partitions community variation among two or three explanatory sets (each a vector of metadata columns).

mp_varpart(gp, groups = list(
  Chemistry = c("pH", "Temp"),
  Habitat   = "SampleType"))

Prevalence and the core microbiome

mp_prevalence() draws a prevalence-abundance scatter ("scatter") or a core-microbiome heatmap across detection thresholds ("core"). The core taxa are labelled automatically; pass color.by to colour points by a taxonomic rank when it has only a handful of levels (colouring by "Phylum" here would add a 60-entry legend, so we leave it off).

mp_prevalence(gp, tax.level = "Phylum")

mp_prevalence(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", plot.type = "core")

Indicator species

mp_indicator() finds taxa significantly associated with groups (via indicspecies). (Requires the indicspecies package.)

mp_indicator(gp, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Genus", top.n = 15)

Differential abundance end to end

mp_run_da() runs a two-group test and returns a tidy table that mp_diff() plots. The default "wilcox" method (Wilcoxon on centred log-ratios) needs no extra packages.

da <- mp_run_da(gp, group.by = "SampleType",
                method = "wilcox", groups = c("Feces", "Soil"))
mp_diff(da, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8)

"deseq2", "aldex2" and "ancombc" wrap the respective Bioconductor packages when installed.

Machine learning

mp_ml() trains a random forest ("rf") or gradient-boosted trees ("xgb") on the feature table. The task is detected from the response: a categorical group.by gives classification, a numeric one regression. (Requires randomForest or xgboost, and pROC for ROC curves.)

gp_genus <- phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Genus")
# Which genera discriminate sample types?
mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "SampleType", method = "rf",
      n.features = 15, seed = 1)

A two-class problem gives an ROC curve from out-of-fold predictions:

two <- phyloseq::subset_samples(gp_genus, SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Soil"))
mp_ml(two, group.by = "SampleType", plot.type = "roc", seed = 1)

A numeric response switches to regression, scored by RMSE / R-squared:

mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "pH", method = "rf",
      plot.type = "prediction", seed = 1)

return.data = TRUE hands back the importance table with the fitted model, cross-validation predictions and metrics attached as attributes:

imp <- mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "SampleType", return.data = TRUE, seed = 1)
head(imp, 3)
#>   feature importance
#> 1  586313 0.09609674
#> 2  295395 0.09173454
#> 3  204889 0.08663335
attr(imp, "metrics")$caption
#> [1] "5-fold CV: accuracy = 73.1%, κ = 0.69"

Coverage plots

mp_coverage() draws sequencing depth across a genome from a data frame, samtools depth, bedGraph/BED files, or a BAM (via Rsamtools).

set.seed(1)
cov <- data.frame(
  contig = rep(c("contig1", "contig2"), each = 100),
  position = rep(seq(1, 10000, length.out = 100), 2),
  depth = c(rpois(100, 60), rpois(100, 25)))
mp_coverage(cov, format = "data.frame")

Circular genome plots

mp_circos() assembles an ideogram with optional coverage, GC, heatmap and annotation tracks plus weighted ribbon links. (Requires circlize.)

genome <- data.frame(contig = c("c1", "c2", "c3"),
                     length = c(8000, 5000, 3000))
covc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genome$contig, function(ct) {
  L <- genome$length[genome$contig == ct]
  data.frame(contig = ct, position = seq(1, L, 50),
             value = runif(length(seq(1, L, 50)), 10, 90))
}))
links <- data.frame(contig1 = "c1", start1 = 500, end1 = 1500,
                    contig2 = "c2", start2 = 1000, end2 = 2000,
                    weight = 0.8)
mp_circos(genome, coverage = covc, links = links, link.by = "weight",
          coverage.type = "area")

Chord diagrams

mp_chord() links the top taxa to the levels of a grouping variable, ribbon width proportional to mean relative abundance. (Requires circlize.)

mp_chord(gp, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 10)
